question:
What is the median of the following data?

57, 96, 60, 91, 69, 50, 72, 16, 78, 73, 55
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Count the total number of given values, which is 11 (an odd number).

The median position is exactly the middle term: (11 + 1) ÷ 2 = 6th position.

To save time, we do not need to sort all numbers. Just identify the 6 smallest values mentally.

The 6 smallest terms in ascending order are: 16, 50, 55, 57, 60, and 69.

The 6th term is 69, which is our required median.

**∴ The correct answer is 69.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Data set: 57, 96, 60, 91, 69, 50, 72, 16, 78, 73, 55

Total number of terms (n) = 11

**Formula Used:**

Median (for an odd number of terms) = Value of the ((n + 1) ÷ 2)th term in the sorted data set.

 Finding the Median

 (6th term out of 11)

**Calculations:**

⇒ First, arrange the data set in ascending order:

⇒ 16, 50, 55, 57, 60, 69, 72, 73, 78, 91, 96

⇒ Number of terms (n) = 11 (which is odd)

⇒ Median position = (11 + 1) ÷ 2 = 12 ÷ 2 = 6th position

⇒ The 6th term in the sorted sequence is 69.

**∴ The correct answer is 69.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean

Mean is the simple average of a data set, calculated by dividing the sum of all observations by the total number of observations.

Median (Even Number of Terms)

When the number of observations (n) is even, the median is the simple average of the (n ÷ 2)th and ((n ÷ 2) + 1)th terms.

Mode

Mode is the value that appears most frequently in a given data set. A dataset may have one mode, multiple modes, or no mode at all.

Range

The range of a data set is the mathematical difference between the highest and lowest values (Range = Maximum value − Minimum value).
